questions.criterion: Yes if the Chamber of Deputies' record of votes (psp.cz) shows the 2027 state budget bill approved in third reading on or before 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET. questions.criterion: Yes if the ČSÚ release of consumer price indices for October 2026 (scheduled for 10 Nov 2026) reports year-on-year CPI growth above 2.5%. The flash estimate of 4 Nov does not count. If the release is delayed beyond 13 Nov 2026 23:59 CET, the flash estimate is used.

The ČSÚ flash estimate for October is due on 4 November and the full release on 10 November. Analysts cite energy prices and core inflation as upside risks (BusinessInfo.cz, 21 Sep 2026). The ČNB target is 2%.

history.note: Prices rose 0.5% month on month in October 2025, a tough base, so October 2026 would need a monthly rise of roughly 0.6% to beat September's 2.5%, and the fuel price cap and diesel excise cut in force through October hit the very item that drove September's jump. A weaker koruna, regulated energy prices, a rebound in food prices or core inflation near 3.1% could still push the figure above 2.5%.
history.note_cs: V říjnu 2025 ceny meziměsíčně stouply o 0,5 %, což je vysoká srovnávací základna, takže letos by musely meziměsíčně vzrůst zhruba o 0,6 %, aby inflace překonala zářijových 2,5 %, a zastropování cen pohonných hmot spolu se snížením spotřební daně z nafty platné po celý říjen dopadá právě na položku, která táhla zářijový skok. Údaj nad 2,5 % by přesto mohla přinést slabší koruna, regulované ceny energií, obrat cen potravin nebo jádrová inflace kolem 3,1 %.

Voluntary agreements with banks, or an increase in the general corporate tax rate, do not count.

questions.background: Andrej Babiš has repeatedly called the banks greedy but has distanced himself from a classic bank tax, floating instead a fund financed from part of bank dividends (Echo24). On 22–23 October 2026 Babiš said he wanted to deal with mortgage prices together with the banks (Echo24), and neither he nor Schillerová announced a levy by 23 October. Kalshi prices at the end of September 2026 implied roughly a 90% chance of Democratic House control (sum of the 'Democratic sweep' and 'D House, R Senate' contracts). Trump was campaigning in a final week of rallies in late October. A Democratic House would end unified Republican control in Washington.

sources.title: Kalshi News: Democrats' Senate control odds jump to 63% (30 Sep 2026)
Khaleej Times: US midterm elections 2026 explainer

history.note: Democrats need a net gain of only a few seats on the 220–215 result of 2024, the president's party has lost House seats in 18 of 20 midterms since 1946, and betting markets strongly favour Democratic control. A correlated polling miss in Republicans' favour or mid-decade redistricting such as Texas's could still keep them below 218 seats.
history.note_cs: Demokratům stačí oproti výsledku z roku 2024 (220:215) čistý zisk jen několika křesel, strana úřadujícího prezidenta ztratila ve Sněmovně reprezentantů křesla v 18 z 20 voleb v polovině funkčního období od roku 1946 a sázkové trhy demokratickou kontrolu jasně favorizují. Pod hranicí 218 křesel by je přesto mohla udržet plošná chyba průzkumů ve prospěch republikánů nebo překreslení volebních obvodů v polovině dekády, například v Texasu.

questions.question: Will the Democrats win control of the US Senate in the 2026 midterm elections?
questions.question_cs: Získají demokraté ve volbách 2026 kontrolu nad Senátem USA?
questions.criterion: Yes if, based on AP race calls and certified results available by 31 Jan 2027 23:59 CET, Democrats and independents caucusing with them hold at least 51 seats in the Senate convening in January 2027 (50 is not enough, as the Vice President is a Republican). Otherwise no.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud podle vyhlášení AP a certifikovaných výsledků dostupných do 31. 1. 2027 ve 23:59 SEČ budou demokraté a s nimi spolupracující nezávislí mít v Senátu, který se sejde v lednu 2027, nejméně 51 křesel (50 nestačí, viceprezident je republikán). Jinak ne.
questions.background: Republicans hold the Senate 53–47 (Washington Post via Kalshi News). Kalshi's Senate market moved from 49% for Democrats on 14 September to 63% on 30 September 2026. Key races include Michigan (El-Sayed v Rogers), Ohio (Sherrod Brown v Jon Husted) and New Hampshire (Pappas v Sununu), with possible Democratic pickups in North Carolina, Maine, Alaska, Iowa and Texas. Runoffs (e.g. Georgia) could push the final call into December.

sources.title: Kalshi News: Democrats' Senate control odds jump to 63% (30 Sep 2026)
Mediaite: Cook shifts four Senate races toward Democrats

base_rate.class: President's party loses at least 4 Senate seats in a midterm, 1946-2022
base_rate.source: Historical midterm Senate seat changes

history.note: Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reach the required 51, early-September polling averages showed them ahead in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas and Alaska and narrowly holding Michigan and New Hampshire, and markets have moved their way since mid-September. Because the path depends on winning several close races at once, a single polling error of two or three points towards Republicans could flip several and leave them short, and a 50–50 Senate would not be enough.
history.note_cs: Demokraté potřebují čistý zisk čtyř křesel, aby dosáhli potřebných 51, průměry průzkumů z počátku září je ukazovaly ve vedení v Severní Karolíně, Maine, Ohiu, Texasu a na Aljašce a při těsném udržení Michiganu a New Hampshiru a trhy se od poloviny září posouvají v jejich prospěch. Protože cesta k většině vyžaduje vyhrát najednou několik těsných soubojů, jediná chyba průzkumů o dva až tři body ve prospěch republikánů by jich mohla zvrátit víc a demokratům by pak většina unikla, přičemž poměr 50:50 nestačí.

questions.question: Will Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win Brazil's presidential runoff on 25 October 2026?

Quaest (17–20 Oct) had Flávio 45%, Lula 44% (Reuters, 21 Oct); Datafolha (20–22 Oct) had them at 50–50 in valid votes (CNN Brasil). The two are due to meet in a final TV Globo debate on the evening of 23 October. Brazil counts electronically and results are usually clear on election night.

CNN Brasil: Datafolha – Flávio and Lula tied at 50% of valid votes
Al Jazeera: Latest poll shows Bolsonaro keeping an edge (16 Oct 2026)

base_rate.source: pipeline/reference-data/poll-error.json (RMS lead error, pp)

history.note: Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round with 47.0% to Lula's 45.2%, most of the remaining votes went to right-leaning candidates, and final polls are tied or slightly favour him (Datafolha 50–50, Quaest 45–44, AtlasIntel 51.1–48.9), while betting markets are far more bearish on Lula. Lula's late momentum, with Datafolha moving from 52–48 for Flávio in early October to a tie, is what could still carry him to victory.

K vítězství by Lulu ještě mohl dovést jeho závěrečný nástup, kdy se průzkum Datafolha posunul z poměru 52:48 pro Flávia na počátku října k vyrovnanému stavu.

history.note: Evening re-forecast with the edition dossier: across the three final-week polls Flávio Bolsonaro leads by about 1.3 points of valid votes (Datafolha 50–50, Quaest and PoderData 51–49), a later AtlasIntel poll still has him ahead, and the forecasters now use the wider pooled poll error rather than Datafolha’s own record. The liquid market (0.235) has not moved. Final Datafolha and Quaest polls are due on 24 October.
history.note_cs: Večerní přepočet s podklady k vydání: ve třech průzkumech z posledního týdne vede Flávio Bolsonaro o zhruba 1,3 bodu platných hlasů (Datafolha 50:50, Quaest a PoderData 51:49), pozdější průzkum AtlasIntel ho rovněž vidí v čele a prognostici nyní počítají s širší souhrnnou chybou průzkumů místo vlastní bilance agentury Datafolha. Likvidní trh (0,235) se nepohnul. Poslední průzkumy Datafolha a Quaest vyjdou 24. října.

questions.question: Will President Herzog task Benjamin Netanyahu with forming Israel's next government by 30 November 2026?
questions.question_cs: Pověří prezident Herzog do 30. listopadu 2026 Benjamina Netanjahua sestavením příští izraelské vlády?
questions.criterion: Yes if the Israeli President's Office (president.gov.il) announces, by 30 Nov 2026 23:59 CET, that Netanyahu has been given the mandate to form a government after the 27 Oct 2026 Knesset election. No if another person receives the first mandate or no mandate is given by then.

questions.background: Israel holds a Knesset election on 27 October 2026. Former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid joined forces in April to challenge Netanyahu (Al Jazeera, 26 Apr 2026). A poll reported by the Jerusalem Post on 21 August gave Netanyahu's bloc 49 seats and the opposition 60, with Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar the largest party at 26 and Likud 20; later polls showed the race tightening. The president consults all Knesset factions and normally tasks the member with the most recommendations within about a week of the official results.

sources.title: Jerusalem Post: poll – opposition 60, coalition 49 (21 Aug 2026)
Al Jazeera: Bennett and Lapid unite to challenge Netanyahu

base_rate.class: Netanyahu receives the first mandate after a Knesset election in which he leads Likud, 2006-2022
base_rate.source: Historical record of presidential mandates (from my own knowledge)

history.note: In the Jerusalem Post average of four mainstream polls Netanyahu's bloc has about 50 seats against about 53 for the Zionist opposition, with Eisenkot's Yashar ahead of Likud, so Eisenkot is likely to collect more recommendations if the opposition, and possibly Arab parties, line up behind him. Netanyahu could still get the mandate, as he did after 7 of the 9 elections he has contested as Likud leader since 2006, if polls underestimate the right or the opposition splits its recommendations between Eisenkot and Bennett.
history.note_cs: V průměru čtyř hlavních průzkumů listu The Jerusalem Post má Netanjahuův blok asi 50 křesel proti zhruba 53 pro sionistickou opozici a Eisenkotova strana Jašar předstihuje Likud, takže více doporučení pravděpodobně získá Eisenkot, pokud se za něj postaví opozice a případně i arabské strany. Netanjahu by přesto mohl pověření dostat, jako se mu to od roku 2006 podařilo po sedmi z devíti voleb, v nichž vedl Likud, pokud průzkumy podcenily pravici nebo pokud opozice rozdělí svá doporučení mezi Eisenkota a Bennetta.

questions.question: Will a new Israeli government win a Knesset confidence vote and be sworn in by 31 January 2027?
questions.question_cs: Získá nová izraelská vláda do 31. ledna 2027 důvěru Knesetu a složí přísahu?
questions.criterion: Yes if the Knesset (main.knesset.gov.il) approves a new government formed after the 27 Oct 2026 election in a confidence vote by 31 Jan 2027 23:59 CET. Otherwise no.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud Kneset (main.knesset.gov.il) do 31. 1. 2027 ve 23:59 SEČ vysloví důvěru nové vládě sestavené po volbách 27. 10. 2026. Jinak ne.
questions.background: The Knesset election is on 27 October 2026. Under Israeli law the tasked member has 28 days, extendable by 14, to form a government, after which the mandate can pass to another member or to the Knesset. After the November 2022 election Netanyahu's government was sworn in on 29 December 2022. Polls through the summer showed neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition reliably above 61 seats without Arab parties (Jerusalem Post, 21 Aug 2026).

sources.title: Jerusalem Post: poll – opposition 60, coalition 49 (21 Aug 2026)
Al Jazeera: Bennett and Lapid unite to challenge Netanyahu

base_rate.class: Israeli elections 2015–2022: government sworn in within 96 days of election
base_rate.source: Wikipedia election/government dates (2015, 2019a, 2019b, 2020, 2021, 2022)

history.note: Polls give neither bloc 61 seats without the Arab parties, a deadlock resembling the two 2019 elections that never produced a government, and the first mandate with its extension runs to about late December, leaving little time for a second attempt before 31 January. A government could still be sworn in on time if the right outperforms the mainstream polls or the opposition builds a coalition relying on Ra'am, as in 2021.
history.note_cs: Podle průzkumů nezíská bez arabských stran 61 křesel žádný blok, což připomíná patovou situaci po obou volbách v roce 2019, z nichž vláda nikdy nevzešla, a první pověření i s prodloužením vyprší zhruba koncem prosince, takže na druhý pokus do 31. ledna zbývá málo času. Vláda by přesto mohla včas složit přísahu, pokud pravice dopadne lépe, než naznačují hlavní průzkumy, nebo pokud opozice sestaví koalici opřenou o stranu Ra'am jako v roce 2021.

questions.question: Will US, Russian and Ukrainian official delegations meet for a new round of trilateral peace talks by 15 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Sejdou se oficiální delegace USA, Ruska a Ukrajiny k novému kolu třístranných mírových jednání do 15. prosince 2026?
questions.criterion: Yes if, by 15 Dec 2026 23:59 CET, the Kremlin (kremlin.ru), the Ukrainian presidency (president.gov.ua) or the White House/State Department confirms that a meeting with official delegations of all three countries has taken place (any level, any venue). Bilateral meetings do not count.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud do 15. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ Kreml (kremlin.ru), ukrajinská prezidentská kancelář (president.gov.ua) nebo Bílý dům/ministerstvo zahraničí USA potvrdí, že se uskutečnilo setkání oficiálních delegací všech tří zemí (na jakékoli úrovni a kdekoli). Dvoustranná setkání se nepočítají.
questions.background: US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on 21 October 2026; Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said Russia agreed in principle to resume three-way talks after 10 November (AP). Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre said talks were likely in mid-November. Earlier trilateral rounds in Abu Dhabi (January and February) and Geneva (February) produced little beyond prisoner exchanges. As of 23 October no date had been named.

sources.title: AP (via AJC): Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg (21 Oct 2026)
Meduza: US, Russia and Ukraine discuss resuming trilateral talks in November
Axios: Witkoff meets Putin

base_rate.class: Announced trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine rounds in 2026 that took place within ~5 weeks of the announced timing
base_rate.source: 2026 record of Abu Dhabi and Geneva rounds plus later postponement (approximate, from my own knowledge)

history.note: After Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin on 21 October, Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said Russia agreed in principle to resume three-way talks after 10 November, with Abu Dhabi under consideration, which leaves about five weeks of slack before 15 December, and the same format already met three times earlier in 2026. The main risk is that Moscow stalls or cancels, as Zelensky warned it has done before, or that the contacts are downgraded to bilateral meetings, which do not count.
history.note_cs: Poté, co se Steve Witkoff 21. října setkal s Vladimirem Putinem, prohlásil poradce Kremlu Jurij Ušakov, že Rusko v zásadě souhlasí s obnovením třístranných jednání po 10. listopadu, přičemž se zvažuje Abú Zabí; do 15. prosince tak zbývá zhruba pět týdnů rezervy a stejný formát se letos sešel už třikrát. Hlavním rizikem je, že Moskva jednání zdrží nebo zruší, jak se podle Zelenského už dříve stalo, případně že kontakty budou omezeny na dvoustranná setkání, která se nepočítají.

questions.question: Will Russia and Ukraine both announce a general ceasefire that takes effect by 31 January 2027?
questions.question_cs: Oznámí Rusko i Ukrajina všeobecné příměří, které vstoupí v platnost do 31. ledna 2027?
questions.criterion: Yes if, by 31 Jan 2027 23:59 CET, both the Kremlin and the Ukrainian presidency officially announce a general ceasefire (covering land, air and sea along the whole front, not limited to energy infrastructure, holidays or a period shorter than 30 days) that has entered into force. Otherwise no.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud do 31. 1. 2027 ve 23:59 SEČ Kreml i ukrajinská prezidentská kancelář oficiálně oznámí všeobecné příměří (na zemi, ve vzduchu i na moři po celé frontě, nikoli jen pro energetickou infrastrukturu, svátky nebo na méně než 30 dní), které vstoupilo v platnost. Jinak ne.
questions.background: No ceasefire is in effect; Russian strikes continued around Witkoff's 21 October 2026 visit to St Petersburg, killing five people (AP). Ushakov said new trilateral talks after 10 November would focus on a post-war security system and called Witkoff's proposals of little real use. Zelensky said he wanted to prepare a leaders' meeting. Earlier 2026 rounds in Abu Dhabi and Geneva produced only prisoner exchanges.

sources.title: AP (via AJC): Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg (21 Oct 2026)
Meduza: trilateral talks could resume in November

base_rate.class: Russia-Ukraine negotiation rounds 2022-2026 that produced a general ceasefire
base_rate.source: public record of Istanbul 2022/2025, Riyadh/Jeddah 2025, Abu Dhabi and Geneva 2026 rounds (approximate count)

history.note: No general ceasefire has been agreed in four and a half years of negotiations, strikes continued around Witkoff's 21 October visit to St Petersburg, and Ushakov frames the next talks around a post-war security system rather than an interim truce. Only a breakthrough at the talks expected after 10 November, producing a ceasefire of at least 30 days along the whole front that both sides announce and that is in force by 31 January, would change this.
history.note_cs: Za čtyři a půl roku vyjednávání nebylo dohodnuto žádné všeobecné příměří, útoky pokračovaly i během Witkoffovy návštěvy Petrohradu 21. října a Ušakov spojuje příští jednání s poválečným bezpečnostním uspořádáním, nikoli s dočasným klidem zbraní. Změnit to by mohl jen průlom na jednáních očekávaných po 10. listopadu, z něhož by vzešlo příměří nejméně na 30 dní po celé frontě, oznámené oběma stranami a platné do 31. ledna.

questions.question: Will the Federal Reserve raise the federal funds target range at its meeting ending 28 October 2026?
questions.question_cs: Zvýší americký Fed na zasedání končícím 28. října 2026 cílové pásmo sazby federálních fondů?
questions.criterion: Yes if the FOMC statement published on federalreserve.gov on 28 Oct 2026 raises the target range for the federal funds rate. Otherwise no.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud prohlášení FOMC zveřejněné na federalreserve.gov 28. 10. 2026 zvýší cílové pásmo sazby federálních fondů. Jinak ne.
questions.background: Kevin Warsh chairs the Fed; he has named October and December as decision points and warned investors against seeking rate clues (investingLive). The September projections' median pointed to a possible hike in December. On 16 October CME FedWatch showed about a 15% probability of an October hike, with markets mostly expecting a hold (Tiger Brokers/itiger, 17 Oct 2026). The war with Iran since February 2026 has pushed up energy prices.

sources.title: Tiger Brokers news: Markets expect a hold in October, Warsh could surprise (17 Oct 2026)
investingLive: Warsh names October and December as decision points

base_rate.class: FOMC decisions with a move priced at 20% or less one week before (approx. 1994-2026)
base_rate.source: approximate: well-known record of no major FOMC surprises vs fed funds futures since 1994; rate changes from pipeline/reference-data/central-banks.json

history.note: Markets have moved firmly towards a hold since a hot September CPI briefly lifted hike bets, Warsh said on 16 October that the data had not changed his view, and the September projections point to December as the natural next step. Only a hawkish surprise from Warsh, who has kept October formally open and gave no signal before the blackout period, would change the outcome, and the Fed rarely surprises markets this way.
history.note_cs: Trhy se od chvíle, kdy vysoká zářijová inflace krátce zvýšila sázky na zvýšení sazeb, výrazně přiklonily k jejich ponechání, Warsh 16. října uvedl, že data jeho názor nezměnila, a zářijové projekce ukazují jako přirozený další krok prosinec. Výsledek by změnilo jen jestřábí překvapení ze strany Warshe, který říjnové zasedání formálně nechal otevřené a před obdobím mlčení nic nenaznačil, a Fed trhy takto překvapuje jen zřídka.

questions.background: The median of the Fed's September 2026 projections pointed to a possible hike in December (Tiger Brokers, 17 Oct 2026). Chair Kevin Warsh has called October and December the key decision points while refusing to pre-commit (investingLive). The ECB, facing 3.8% euro-area inflation, is also widely expected to hike in December. Energy prices have been driven up by the Iran war and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.

investingLive: Warsh names October and December as decision points

Easing energy prices after any de-escalation with Iran, weak payrolls, political pressure on Warsh or a surprise October hike that pre-empts December could still lead to a hold.

K ponechání sazeb by přesto mohlo vést zlevnění energií po případné deeskalaci s Íránem, slabá data o zaměstnanosti, politický tlak na Warshe nebo nečekané zvýšení v říjnu, které by prosincový krok předběhlo.

questions.background: The war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026; a June interim ceasefire collapsed (bdnews24/AFP, 12 Oct 2026). Qatar and Pakistan are passing messages; Iran says the US response did not meet its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and returning to talks, while Washington wants the nuclear file addressed first. Iran told Pakistan on 20 October there would be no talks until its demands were met (TimesLIVE), and Reuters reported Iran was prolonging the stalemate to influence the US midterms.

A poll reported by Novinite on 22 October gave her 43.4% against 28.9% for Andrey Gyurov (PP–DB). The main risks are anti-Radev voters consolidating behind Gyurov in the likely 1 November runoff and the Central Election Commission declaring the result after the 3 November deadline.

agents.reason: First-round leaders have won every Bulgarian runoff since 1992 and Iotova leads in four of five parallel counts, but the margin is near zero (one count has Gyurov ahead), so the base rate must be shrunk heavily toward a coin flip; Vazrazhdane's 12-15% electorate is more likely to break toward the Radev-backed Iotova than PP-DB's Gyurov, and CIK normally declares within 48 hours, well before 3 Nov.

The first round is almost a tie: Iotova leads in four of five parallel counts by about 0.5 to 3 points, and Market Links has Gyurov ahead. Kostadinov's 12 to 15% Vazrazhdane voters are nationalist and Russia-friendly, so they should lean towards the Radev-backed Iotova rather than PP-DB's Gyurov, though very low turnout and anti-establishment consolidation make the runoff genuinely uncertain. There is a small extra risk that the CEC declares the result after 3 Nov.

The pre-election 43-29 poll was badly wrong: exit polls and parallel counts have Iotova 32-35 vs Gyurov 31.6-33.5 with one agency putting Gyurov ahead, so the 7/7 'first-round leader always wins' base rate rests on a 1-3 point lead and 22% turnout; GERB and Peevski's DPS votes (anti-Radev machine blocs) plus any PP-DB mobilisation give Gyurov a plausible path, Kostadinov (12-15%) is personally hostile to Radev and will not endorse for free, and CIK must publish a decision declaring her elected by 3 Nov 23:59 CET, about 48 hours after polls close, a small technical risk. Against that, Vazrazhdane voters' second preference is far closer to Radev's camp than to a PP-DB liberal, BSP and nationalist remnants flow to her, and incumbency plus Radev's machine still make her the modest favourite.

Anchored on Polymarket at 0.715 (vol 0.73M; Kalshi 0.79 on thin volume). The first round was a near tie, 4 of 5 parallel counts have Iotova ahead, and the 1 Nov runoff likely depends on Vazrazhdane voters, who probably lean to her rather than PP-DB's Gyurov. I trimmed slightly for the small risk that CIK publishes after the 3 Nov deadline.

Iotova's first-round lead is far smaller than the 43% polled (about 32-35% against Gyurov at 31-33.5%), and one agency has Gyurov ahead. The 12-15% Kostadinov vote and anti-Radev consolidation make the runoff close, but the first-round leader has won every runoff since 1992 and four of five parallel counts have her first.

history.note: The first round on 25 October was far closer than the polls: exit polls and parallel counts put Iliana Iotova at 32–35% and Andrey Gyurov at 31–33.5% (one agency has Gyurov ahead), on a turnout of about 22%; the 1 November runoff is likely to turn on Vazrazhdane voters.
history.note_cs: První kolo 25. října dopadlo mnohem těsněji, než ukazovaly průzkumy: podle odhadů u volebních místností a paralelních sčítání má Iliana Iotova 32–35 % a Andrej Gyurov 31–33,5 % (jedna agentura vidí v čele Gyurova) při účasti kolem 22 %. Druhé kolo 1. listopadu nejspíš rozhodnou voliči Obrození.

questions.question: Will the French government invoke Article 49.3 of the constitution on the 2027 state budget bill by 31 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Použije francouzská vláda do 31. prosince 2026 u návrhu státního rozpočtu na rok 2027 článek 49.3 ústavy?
questions.criterion: Yes if, by 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET, the Prime Minister engages the government's responsibility under Article 49(3) on the projet de loi de finances pour 2027 (any part or reading), as recorded by the Assemblée nationale (assemblee-nationale.fr). Use of 49.3 only on the social security budget (PLFSS) does not count.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud do 31. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ premiér podle čl. 49 odst. 3 spojí odpovědnost vlády s návrhem zákona o státním rozpočtu na rok 2027 (jakoukoli částí či čtením), podle záznamu Národního shromáždění (assemblee-nationale.fr). Použití 49.3 jen u rozpočtu sociálního zabezpečení (PLFSS) se nepočítá.
questions.background: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's minority government opened floor debate on the 2027 budget on 13 October 2026 after the finance committee rejected the revenue part on 9 October (LCP). Ministers have not ruled out 49.3 or ordinances; LFI says it will table a censure motion if 49.3 is used, and the Socialists, now backing Raphaël Glucksmann of Place Publique as presidential candidate, threaten censure unless the text changes. Lecornu had renounced 49.3 in autumn 2025 but used it in January 2026 to pass the 2026 budget. France is also facing weekly gilets jaunes protests since 17 October.

sources.title: LCP: 2027 budget – the government on a knife-edge (12 Oct 2026)
La Libre: Lecornu to use 49.3 to pass the 2026 budget (19 Jan 2026)
LCP: Budget 2027 dossier

base_rate.class: Years 2022–2025 in which 49.3 was used on the PLF before 31 Dec
base_rate.source: 2022, 2023 yes (Borne); 2024 no (Barnier used it only on PLFSS before being censured); 2025 no (January 2026)

history.note: Ministers call adoption by vote "très difficile" and have not ruled out Article 49.3, the Assembly's 40-day first-reading limit (around 10 November) and the 70-day point after which ordinances become possible (around 10 December) both fall within the window, and Lecornu used 49.3 for the 2026 budget. But in the last cycle he waited, bridged the year-end with a special law and invoked 49.3 only in January 2026, and a repeat of that sequence or the use of ordinances would resolve the question negatively.
history.note_cs: Ministři označují schválení rozpočtu hlasováním za „velmi obtížné“ a použití článku 49.3 nevyloučili, do sledovaného období spadá 40denní lhůta pro první čtení v Národním shromáždění (kolem 10. listopadu) i 70denní lhůta, po níž lze rozpočet zavést nařízeními (kolem 10. prosince), a Lecornu článek 49.3 použil u rozpočtu na rok 2026. V minulém cyklu však vyčkával, konec roku překlenul zvláštním zákonem a k článku 49.3 sáhl až v lednu 2026; opakování tohoto postupu nebo použití nařízení by otázku rozhodlo záporně.

questions.question: Will the French National Assembly adopt a motion of censure against Sébastien Lecornu's government by 31 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Přijme francouzské Národní shromáždění do 31. prosince 2026 návrh na vyslovení nedůvěry vládě Sébastiena Lecornua?
questions.criterion: Yes if the Assemblée nationale adopts a motion de censure (by an absolute majority of the members of the Assembly, as required by Article 49 of the Constitution) against the Lecornu government by 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET, as recorded on assemblee-nationale.fr. No if no motion is adopted, or if the government leaves office in another way.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud Národní shromáždění do 31. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ přijme návrh na vyslovení nedůvěry (absolutní většinou členů Národního shromáždění, jak vyžaduje článek 49 ústavy) vládě Lecornua, podle záznamu na assemblee-nationale.fr. Ne, pokud žádný návrh přijat nebude nebo pokud vláda skončí jiným způsobem.
questions.background: Lecornu's government has no majority and needs either the Socialists or the RN to abstain to survive budget votes (LCP, 12 Oct 2026). The RN says it will not censure automatically but calls pension de-indexation a red line; the Socialists say there will be censure unless the text changes; LFI will table a motion if 49.3 is used. Several censure motions were rejected during the 2026 budget process in January–February 2026. The government is also contending with violent gilets jaunes protests that began on 17 October.

sources.title: LCP: 2027 budget – the government on a knife-edge (12 Oct 2026)
Blick: Assembly rejects a third censure motion (2026)
Le Petit Journal: Political crisis and violence in France – latest

base_rate.class: Fifth Republic censure motions adopted
base_rate.source: Assemblée nationale records (2 adopted: 1962, 2024)

history.note: A censure motion has passed only twice in the Fifth Republic, in 1962 and against Barnier in 2024, every motion against Lecornu has failed (with 271 and 256 votes against the 289 needed), and success would require the Socialists and the RN to vote together, which both have pre-election reasons to avoid. A 49.3 on a budget that keeps pension de-indexation, the RN's red line, without the changes the Socialists demand is the most likely trigger that could change this.
history.note_cs: Návrh na vyslovení nedůvěry prošel za páté republiky jen dvakrát, v roce 1962 a v roce 2024 proti Barnierovi, všechny návrhy proti Lecornuovi neuspěly (získaly 271 a 256 hlasů při potřebných 289) a úspěch by vyžadoval společné hlasování socialistů a Národního sdružení, kterému se obě strany mají před prezidentskými volbami důvod vyhnout. Nejpravděpodobnějším spouštěčem změny by bylo použití článku 49.3 u rozpočtu, který zachová zmrazení valorizace důchodů, tedy červenou linii Národního sdružení, a nebude obsahovat změny požadované socialisty.

questions.question: Will the EU Council adopt a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia by 31 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Přijme Rada EU do 31. prosince 2026 22. balík sankcí proti Rusku?
questions.criterion: Yes if a Council of the EU press release (consilium.europa.eu) or the Official Journal records the formal adoption of the 22nd package of restrictive measures against Russia by 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET. Agreement by ambassadors (Coreper) alone does not count.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud tisková zpráva Rady EU (consilium.europa.eu) nebo Úřední věstník do 31. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ zaznamená formální přijetí 22. balíku restriktivních opatření proti Rusku. Pouhá shoda velvyslanců (Coreper) se nepočítá.
questions.background: The EU adopted its 21st sanctions package against Russia in July 2026 (Mayer Brown, 24 Jul). Bloomberg reported the EU aimed to adopt a 22nd package in October (via TASS); a separate listing of about 1,600 entities on 12 October was not the 22nd package. On 19 October Commission spokespeople said only that work was ongoing and gave no date (Charter97). A Zelensky adviser said adoption could come in November (UA.News). Sanctions require unanimity among the 27 member states.

sources.title: Mayer Brown: EU adopts 21st package against Russia (24 Jul 2026)
Charter97: Commission working on next sanctions package (19 Oct 2026)
UA.News: EU may adopt 22nd package in November

base_rate.class: Gaps between consecutive EU Russia sanctions packages <= 5.2 months, 2022-2026
base_rate.source: dossier-R

history.note: Three months after the 21st package the Commission had still not presented the 22nd by 19 October and gave no date, so a proposal in November would leave only weeks for unanimous agreement, while recent packages have taken from five weeks to more than two and a half months, with Hungary, Slovakia and Greece holding up earlier ones. A pre-Christmas push like the December adoptions of 2023 and 2024 could still deliver it by year-end, though oil measures during an energy-price crisis invite fresh vetoes.
history.note_cs: Komise ani tři měsíce po přijetí 21. balíku do 19. října 22. balík nepředložila a neuvedla žádné datum, takže při návrhu v listopadu by na jednomyslnou shodu zbývalo jen několik týdnů, zatímco nedávné balíky trvaly od pěti týdnů po více než dva a půl měsíce a Maďarsko, Slovensko a Řecko ty předchozí zdržovaly. Přijetí do konce roku by přesto mohl přinést předvánoční tlak, jako tomu bylo při prosincovém schválení balíků v letech 2023 a 2024, opatření týkající se ropy v době energetické krize však mohou vyvolat nová veta.

questions.question: Will EU leaders reach political agreement on the 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework by 31 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Dosáhnou lídři EU do 31. prosince 2026 politické dohody o víceletém finančním rámci na roky 2028–2034?
questions.criterion: Yes if European Council conclusions or a statement by its President published on consilium.europa.eu by 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET record agreement among all 27 heads of state or government on the overall size and structure of the 2028–2034 MFF. Partial agreements or progress reports do not count.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud závěry Evropské rady nebo prohlášení jejího předsedy zveřejněné na consilium.europa.eu do 31. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ zaznamenají dohodu všech 27 hlav států či vlád o celkovém objemu a struktuře víceletého finančního rámce 2028–2034. Dílčí dohody ani zprávy o pokroku se nepočítají.
questions.background: The October 2026 EU summit ended inconclusively on the 2028–2034 budget; the Irish presidency's proposal to cut the total by €141 billion was largely rejected (Euronews, 15 Oct). Council President António Costa is taking over the negotiations and stepping up meetings with all delegations (Eunews, 21 Oct), with a special summit planned for 26 November. Summit conclusions softened the year-end target, saying only that a deal before the end of 2026 would allow legislation to be adopted in 2027. The previous MFF was agreed on 21 July 2020, about five and a half months before it started.

sources.title: Euronews: Inconclusive sparring at EU summit puts budget timeline into question (15 Oct 2026)
Eunews: Costa steps up work on the multiannual budget (21 Oct 2026)

base_rate.class: MFF political agreements reached within 18 months of Commission proposal
base_rate.source: 2007–13, 2014–20, 2021–27 MFF timelines (general knowledge)

history.note: The October summit ended inconclusively, the Irish presidency's €141 billion cut was largely rejected and leaders softened the year-end target, while previous MFF deals took 20–26 months from the Commission's proposal against about 17 months for a December 2026 deal. Only a breakthrough on António Costa's new negotiating box at the 26 November special summit or the December European Council could produce an agreement this year.
history.note_cs: Říjnový summit skončil bez výsledku, návrh irského předsednictví na snížení o 141 miliard eur byl z velké části odmítnut a lídři zmírnili cíl dohodnout se do konce roku, přičemž předchozí dohody o víceletém finančním rámci trvaly od návrhu Komise 20 až 26 měsíců, kdežto dohoda v prosinci 2026 by přišla zhruba po 17 měsících. Dohodu by letos mohl přinést jen průlom nad novým vyjednávacím návrhem Antónia Costy na mimořádném summitu 26. listopadu nebo na prosincové Evropské radě.

questions.question: Will the Chamber of Deputies pass the government bill abolishing the ČT and ČRo licence fees in third reading by 31 January 2027?
questions.question_cs: Schválí Poslanecká sněmovna ve třetím čtení vládní návrh zákona o zrušení koncesionářských poplatků za Českou televizi a Český rozhlas do 31. ledna 2027?
questions.criterion: Yes if the Chamber of Deputies' record of votes (psp.cz) shows that the government bill replacing the ČT and ČRo licence fees with state-budget funding (approved by the cabinet on 15 June 2026) was passed in third reading, with or without amendments, on or before 31 Jan 2027 23:59 CET. Approval by the Senate, a Chamber override of a Senate rejection, or the president's signature are not required. A partial bill that only exempts some groups from fees while keeping the fees does not count. No if the bill is rejected, withdrawn or not voted on in third reading by then.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud záznam hlasování Poslanecké sněmovny (psp.cz) ukáže, že vládní návrh zákona, který nahrazuje koncesionářské poplatky za ČT a ČRo financováním ze státního rozpočtu (vláda jej schválila 15. června 2026), byl schválen ve třetím čtení, s pozměňovacími návrhy či bez nich, nejpozději 31. 1. 2027 ve 23:59 SEČ. Schválení Senátem, přehlasování Senátu ani podpis prezidenta se nevyžadují. Novela, která poplatky zachová a jen od nich osvobodí některé skupiny, se nepočítá. Ne, pokud bude návrh zamítnut, stažen nebo do termínu nebude ve třetím čtení odhlasován.
questions.background: On 15 June 2026 the Babiš cabinet approved a bill to abolish licence fees and fund Česká televize (CZK 5.74 bn) and Český rozhlas (CZK 2.065 bn) from the state budget, about CZK 1.35 bn less than now, from January 2027 (Novinky, 15 Jun). In August the bill was still awaiting first reading; Finance Minister Schillerová and Culture Minister Klempíř would not guarantee the 1 January start, the Senate and President Pavel have criticised the bill and the opposition has promised obstruction (Echo24, 25 Aug). On 23 October the coalition pushed the bill onto the Chamber's agenda and debate began, with the opposition promising obstruction; ČT and ČRo employees announced a one-day strike for 3 November (Echo24 headlines, 23 Oct). The ANO–SPD–Motoristé coalition has a majority, but the 2027 budget's second and third readings (third reading planned for 2 December) compete for floor time.

sources.title: Novinky 15 Jun 2026: Vláda schválila zrušení koncesionářských poplatků
Echo24 25 Aug 2026: Poplatky za ČT a ČRo měly skončit od ledna. Vláda připouští průtahy (sidebar 23 Oct: Sněmovna projednává zrušení poplatků; opozice slibuje obstrukce)
CNN Prima News: Koncesionářské poplatky úplně zrušíme, řekl Klempíř

history.note: The coalition has a majority and pushed the bill onto the agenda on 23 October, but first reading has only just begun under announced obstruction, the committee stage takes weeks and the 2027 budget occupies the floor until its third reading on 2 December, so a third-reading vote by 31 January needs fixed-time voting or similar procedural force.
history.note_cs: Koalice má většinu a 23. října prosadila návrh na program, první čtení však teprve začalo za ohlášené obstrukce, výborové projednání trvá týdny a do třetího čtení rozpočtu 2. prosince zabírá jednací čas rozpočet 2027, takže hlasování ve třetím čtení do 31. ledna vyžaduje pevné hlasování nebo podobný procedurální nástroj.

questions.question: Will Miloš Vystrčil be re-elected President of the Senate by 31 December 2026?
questions.question_cs: Bude Miloš Vystrčil do 31. prosince 2026 znovu zvolen předsedou Senátu?
questions.criterion: Yes if, on or before 31 Dec 2026 23:59 CET, the Senate elects Miloš Vystrčil as its president for the term beginning after the October 2026 Senate elections, as recorded on senat.cz or reported by ČTK. No if another senator is elected, or if no president is elected by then.
questions.criterion_cs: Ano, pokud Senát nejpozději 31. 12. 2026 ve 23:59 SEČ zvolí Miloše Vystrčila svým předsedou pro období po senátních volbách v říjnu 2026, podle senat.cz nebo ČTK. Ne, pokud bude zvolen jiný senátor nebo pokud do termínu předseda zvolen nebude.
questions.background: Miloš Vystrčil (ODS) has led the Senate since 2020. After the October 2026 elections the joint ODS–TOP 09 club remains the largest, although STAN won the most seats (10 plus independent Marek Ošťádal); ANO won no seats. STAN leader Vít Rakušan said STAN has no problem with Vystrčil keeping the post, ODS leader Martin Kupka said Vystrčil will remain, and STAN wants to keep Jiří Drahoš as first deputy (Seznam Zprávy, 17 Oct). New senators take the oath on 19 November and the leadership vote is due in November; the ODS–TOP 09 club is expected to nominate Vystrčil again (ČT24, 20 Oct). He would be a prominent critic of the Babiš government from the second-highest constitutional post.

sources.title: Seznam Zprávy 17 Oct 2026: Neúprosná „obhajovací matematika“ STAN. O vedení Senátu ODS nepřipraví
ČT24 20 Oct 2026: Senát čekají personální šachy a úvahy o novém výboru

base_rate.class: Sitting Senate presidents seeking re-election after a biennial election with their club still largest (Vystrčil 2020, 2022, 2024)
base_rate.source: https://www.e15.cz/vysledky-voleb-a-referend/volby-do-senatu/vystrcil-zrejme-zustane-v-cele-senatu-ma-podporu-stan-i-koalice-top-09-s-ods-1374134

history.note: Vystrčil was re-elected after each of the last three Senate elections, his ODS–TOP 09 club remains the largest, and both STAN’s leader Vít Rakušan and ODS leader Martin Kupka have backed him; the vote is due in November after the new senators take the oath on 19 November. The residual risk is a surprise rival in the secret ballot.
history.note_cs: Vystrčil byl znovu zvolen po každých z posledních tří senátních voleb, jeho klub ODS a TOP 09 zůstává nejsilnější a podpořili ho předseda STAN Vít Rakušan i předseda ODS Martin Kupka; volba se čeká v listopadu po složení slibu nových senátorů 19. listopadu. Zbývajícím rizikem je překvapivý protikandidát v tajné volbě.
